name.es-ES: Audi, filia (1556): Avisos y reglas cristianas
name.en-US: Audi, Filia (1556): Christian Counsels and Rules
name.pt-BR: Audi, filia (1556): Avisos e regras cristãs

description.es-ES: Primera redacción impresa del «Audi, filia» (Alcalá de Henares, Juan de Brocar, 1556): «Avisos y reglas cristianas para los que desean servir a Dios, aprovechando en el camino espiritual, compuestas sobre aquel verso de David: Audi, filia, et vide, et inclina aurem tuam», con la dedicatoria al conde de Palma, la Breve regla de vida cristiana y los seis capítulos mayores sobre las seis palabras del verso. Edición de Luis Sala Balust (1963) con ortografía del siglo XVI; los epígrafes entre corchetes son del editor. Distinta de la redacción de 1574, que tiene su propio libro.
description.en-US: The first printed redaction of the «Audi, filia» (Alcalá de Henares, Juan de Brocar, 1556): «Christian counsels and rules for those who wish to serve God, advancing on the spiritual way, composed on David's verse: Audi, filia, et vide, et inclina aurem tuam», with the dedication to the Count of Palma, the Brief Rule of Christian Life and six major parts on the six words of the verse. Luis Sala Balust's edition (1963) in sixteenth-century spelling; the headings in brackets are the editor's. Distinct from the 1574 redaction, which has its own book.
description.pt-BR: Primeira redação impressa do «Audi, filia» (Alcalá de Henares, 1556): avisos e regras cristãs sobre o verso de Davi, com a dedicatória ao conde de Palma e a Breve regra de vida cristã.

sources.edition: Maestro Juan de Ávila, Avisos y reglas cristianas sobre aquel verso de David «Audi, filia», ed. Luis Sala Balust, Barcelona: Juan Flors, 1963 (Espirituales españoles, serie A, tomo X); archive.org scan from Princeton Theological Seminary, OCR.
sources.description: The text of the 1556 Alcalá edition, as edited by Sala Balust: dedication, bookseller's note, Breve regla and the six parts, split at the editor's headings. Not imported: the editor's introduction, the three appendices (Pedro Fernández de Córdoba's life of doña Sancha Carrillo, the censure, the 1573 text) and the indexes. The editor's scripture-reference notes are listed at the end of the chapters where the OCR kept them (about two thirds); their markers in the text are lost. Folio marks of the 1556 print and its line-break slashes are removed.
sources.tierEvidence: The text is Ávila's of 1556 (public domain); the scan is freely posted on archive.org with no rights statement.
